name: BlackSea Technologies
note: Per-company dossier. Every field carries its source and retrieval date. Absent facts are listed as gaps, not estimated.

identity.founded_basis: Roots in Maritime Applied Physics Corporation, Baltimore, 1986. The companies combined through acquisitions in 2022 to form BlackSea Technologies.
identity.employees: about 235, with staff also in Florida, North Carolina and California
identity.description_by_company: Building the state of the art in AI-enabled manned and unmanned teams.

axis_evidence.escort: It's larger size allows Comet to carry a variety of payloads to fit a multitude of missions, including C-UAS, ISR, high value escort, and mine countermeasures.
axis_evidence.escort_company_wording: The Comet page names high-value-unit escort in its mission list.
axis_evidence.uncrewed: GARC, Chaser, Comet, NightTrain and SPDS are all uncrewed surface platforms.
axis_evidence.security: Named missions include ISR, MCM, strike, interdiction, AAW/C-UAS, ASW, SUW and EW.
axis_evidence.commercial: No source found describes commercial or civil customers. Every named customer is the US Navy.

reclassified.reason: The escort axis was recorded false. Naval News of 10 May 2026 and BlackSea's own Comet page both name high-value escort as a Comet mission.

ownership.structure: Razor's Edge founded BlackSea as a flagship platform company; not venture rounds

pending_acquisition.value: AEVEX record in this library carries 'agreement to acquire for up to $650 million'
pending_acquisition.status: Announced, not confirmed closed as of 2026-09-03.

ownership.funding_note: No venture rounds found. Backed as a private-equity platform company rather than through priced rounds.

contracts.customer: US Navy, PMO 314 Logistics Over the Shore
contracts.scope: Build and support the Seabased Petroleum Distribution System, including up to five SPDS units and support equipment.

contracts.date_basis: A government database listed the ceiling; the article does not date the award itself.

contracts.scope: Begin building five GARCs. Held by predecessor MAPC.

platforms.name: Comet
platforms.endurance: 1,000 nmi with 3,000 lb payload at 40 kn in Sea State 3; 500 nmi with 7,500 lb at 20 kn
platforms.role_by_company: AAW/C-UAS, MCM, SUW, ASW, EW, MDA, ISR, high-value-unit escort, distributed maritime operations

platforms.name: Chaser (GARC Block II)
platforms.endurance: 1,900 nmi at 5 kn; 875 nmi at 22 kn
platforms.role_by_company: MDA, distributed ISR, comms relay, strike coordination, contested logistics

platforms.name: GARC
platforms.endurance: about 1,000 miles on a tank of diesel
platforms.role_by_company: ISR, comms relay, MCM, strike, survey, interdiction

platforms.name: NightTrain
platforms.payload: about 71 tons; up to 53 linear feet of ISO containers

platforms.name: SPDS
platforms.payload: 900 LT lightship, 125 ft operating depth, 45 ft width
platforms.role_by_company: Autonomous expeditionary bulk fuel distribution from offshore to forces ashore

platforms.name: Mainstay
platforms.role_by_company: Open autonomy architecture connecting autonomy software, vessel controls, sensors, payloads, comms and C2. Not a vessel.

leadership.title: Founder and president of predecessor Maritime Applied Physics Corporation

quotes.text: It's larger size allows Comet to carry a variety of payloads to fit a multitude of missions, including C-UAS, ISR, high value escort, and mine countermeasures.

articles.title: New Comet and Chaser USV by BlackSea Technologies
key_points: Comet mission set explicitly includes high value escort.
Chaser range roughly 600-800 nmi at 20 knots per this report, which differs from the company figures.

articles.title: Baltimore naval drone boats: BlackSea Technologies
key_points: $2M Navy contract in 2022 for five GARCs.
Government database lists a GARC contract worth up to $213M.

values.value: 1,900 nmi at 5 kn; 875 nmi at 22 kn

conflicts.resolution: Unresolved. The company figure and the Naval News figure are not reconcilable at comparable speeds.

gaps: No commercial or civil customer is named in any source. Every named customer is the US Navy.
No unit price is published for any platform.
No venture funding rounds exist to compare against peers; the company is a private-equity platform company.
The AEVEX acquisition was announced 12 August 2026 and expected to close in September 2026. Whether it has closed is not confirmed here.
Escort appears as one mission in a long defence mission list, not as a service sold to shipowners.
